 15s ago 12.28 EDT Kamari Doyle has put Leicester back in front against Stevenage in League One and Salford have equalised at home against Exeter.
 Share 2m ago 12.27 EDT In the Championship, Swansea are now 4-0 up against Blackburn, Wolves are beating Cardiff 3-0 and Bolton have turned it around against Bristol City to lead 2-1.
 Share 3m ago 12.25 EDT Goal! Coventry 3-1 Sunderland (Le Fée 67, pen)
 No mistake from Le Fée as he cuts the lead from the spot.
 Share 5m ago 12.24 EDT Penalty to Sunderland!
 After a length VAR check Sunderland are awarded a penalty for handball, there was a moment of slapstick as the touchline screen froze while they were checking for offisde in the buildup.
 Share 7m ago 12.21 EDT Goal! Hull 1-1 Ipswich (Iroegbunam 58)
 After missing a number of chances in the first half Ipswich have allowed Hull back into this one. it’s bizarre, Iroegbunam is allowed to keep going and going, unchallenged and eventually beats Walton with a low strike.
 Share 9m ago 12.19 EDT Brentford 1-0 Nottingham Forest 
 I mentioned Forest’s odd form pre-match. The Bees still lead this one, but neither side has had a shot on target.
 Share 12m ago 12.16 EDT Having had a second goal disallowed before half-time Southampton now have their 2-0 lead against QPR, Cameron Bragg has got it.
 Share 14m ago 12.14 EDT A fitba update from Simon McMahon (thanks, Simon): “Only two Scottish Premiership games today because of the League Cup semis this weekend. Kilmarnock currently lead 10-man St. Johnstone 2-1, while Motherwell v St Mirren is goalless. The first of those League Cup semi finals is a team time kick-off and features Rangers v crisis club one Aberdeen, whose fans have never really taken to manager Stephen Robinson. An Edinburgh derby tomorrow between Hearts and crisis club two Hibs will decide the other finalist.”
 Share 16m ago 12.13 EDT Goal! Coventry 3-0 Sunderland (Rudoni 52)
 A huge slice of fortune in this but the Sky Blues are pulling away. It’s lovely buildup from Coventry to work it into the Sunderland half but Rudoni’s shot has not right to go in from there, it’s low and not particularly vicious until it takes a big deflection off of Omar Alderete to beat Roefs.
 Share 20m ago 12.08 EDT Great game at the London Stadium, it’s now 2-1 to West Brom, Jimmy-Jay Morgan has put the Baggies back in front.
 Share 21m ago 12.07 EDT Manchester City 0-1 Brighton 
 Big chance for Brighton for to go 2-0 up at the Etihad but De Cuyper has blazed over when found in acres of space in the City box. Will they pay for that?
 Share 23m ago 12.05 EDT Early goal in League One, Liam Kelly has put into his own net to give Luton a 2-0 lead at Peterborough.
 Share 24m ago 12.04 EDT Peeeeeeeep!

 Share 42m ago 11.47 EDT In League Two, league leaders Salford are 1-0 down against Exeter, Sonny Cox putting the Grecians ahead. Ten-man Rotherham so far are hanging on against Swindon.
 View image in fullscreen Sonny Cox slots the ball home to give Exeter City the lead. Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock Share Updated at  12.07 EDT 44m ago 11.45 EDT Talking of Boro, Will Lankshear has made it 2-0 against Charlton. That’s his 12th fo the season.
 Share 46m ago 11.42 EDT Swansea have scored a quickfire double to take a 3-0 lead against Blackburn. The Swans are flying high in the Championship, sitting second just behind Boro.

 Awoniyi robs O’Nien in the Sunderland half and just goes at the heart of the Black Cats defence before finding the bottom corner with a bit of a scruffy finish, great goal though.

Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock Share Updated at  12.05 EDT 51m ago 11.37 EDT Jarrod Bowen has equalised for West Ham against the Baggies, the England international drives in from the right and hits a low shot at the near post which sneaks past O’Leary in the West Brom goal.
 View image in fullscreen Jarrod Bowen fires home the Hammers’ equaliser. Photograph: Gareth Fuller/PA View image in fullscreen Bowen celebrates restoring parity. Photograph: Gareth Fuller/PA Share Updated at  12.01 EDT 54m ago 11.35 EDT Goal! Bournemouth 1-0 Leeds (Evanilson 31)

Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Which Sakamoto is pretty happy about. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock Share Updated at  11.46 EDT 1h ago 11.17 EDT Deeper mire for Derby, Lisbie has his second for Millwall, 2-0 there. Elsewhere in the Championship, Southampton have taken the lead against QPR, Swansea are 1-0 up against Blackburn and Wolves have already struck twice without reply against Cardiff.
 View image in fullscreen Kyrell Lisbie of Millwall celebrates scoring his second goal. Photograph: Sean Ryan/Shutterstock Share Updated at  11.38 EDT 1h ago 11.15 EDT 11min: VAR check on a goal for Dominic Calvert-Lewin at the Vitality, the Leeds bundled it in from close range but it’s come off his bicep. That’s not going to stand.
 Share 1h ago 11.13 EDT Goal! Manchester City 0-1 Brighton (Ayari 11)
 Dunk pings the ball out to Gomez who sweeps in a low cross, it ricochets off De Cuyper and falls to Ayari, who can’t miss. Brighton’s third goal at the Etihad this week.
 View image in fullscreen Brighton’s Yasin Ayari tucks the ball home to give the visitors the lead at the Etihad. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA View image in fullscreen Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas and Yasin Ayar (right) celebrate. Photograph: Jon Super/AP View image in fullscreen Brighton fans, including a Harold Bishop lookalike (left), celebrate the Seagulls taking the lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  11.47 EDT 1h ago 11.10 EDT In League Two, Accrington are 1-0 up against Northampton, Walsall have taken the lead at Colchester, while Gillingham are in front Shrewsbury. Jili Buyabu has earned an early birth at the County Ground, do they have baths? Rotherham now facing an uphill battle against Swindon.
 Share 1h ago 11.07 EDT Millwall 1-0 Derby 
 The Rams are in deep trouble, with just one win so far this season in the Championship and now they have gone down early at the Den. Kyrell Lisbie with the opener.
 View image in fullscreen Kyrell Lisbie of Millwall scores the opening goal. Photograph: Sean Ryan/Shutterstock Share Updated at  11.38 EDT 1h ago 11.05 EDT A couple more League One goals to fill you in on, MK Dons have gone 1-0 up against Doncaster and Luton are a goal to the good on the road at Luton.

 Sammy Braybrooke has given the home side an early lead at the King Power. The Foxes are picking up their form after a shaky start to the season.

 We are underway in the 3pm kick-offs.
 Share 2h ago 10.57 EDT The teams are coming out and we are moments away from kick-off around the grounds.
 Share 2h ago 10.55 EDT Jacob Steinberg Get ready for another week of agonising over the sorry state of Manchester United. The legends of old will rage, clips of a fuming Gary Neville will fly around social media, the airwaves will reverberate with complaints from angry supporters and by the time United play again there is every chance a new manager will be in the dugout.
 There were echoes of Erik ten Hag’s final game in charge as the walls closed in on Michael Carrick at Stamford Bridge. United missed a series of golden chances when the scores were level, just as they did when Ten Hag lost to West Ham a day before his sacking two years ago, and Chelsea made the most of the reprieve after initially delivering a performance so bad it had you worrying for the nascent Xabi Alonso project.
 Read Jacob’s rull report from Stamford Bridge: 
 Manchester United crisis deepens with Chelsea defeat and Martínez red card Read more Share 2h ago 10.38 EDT It’s all over at Stamford Bridge, Lisandro Martínez earned a moronic red card as Manchester United failed to build on a positive first half to lose 2-0. Scott Murray has the reaction:
 Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United: Premier League – live reaction Read more View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick couldn’t even look at Lisandro Martínez after the Manchester United defender was sent off for a second bookable offence. Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images Share 2h ago 10.34 EDT Nottingham Forest are a strange proposition. Lots of quality players but they’ve only won one Premier League game so far this season. They’ve only conceded 10 goals – an Oliver Glasner trademark is defensive organisation – but Liam Delap is yet to fire and today they face another well-organised defence in Brentford. Every chance Forest start November in the bottom three, a position which has typically cost the manager his job. Forest fans, what do you make of the season so far?
 Share 2h ago 10.07 EDT Will Unwin I am at the big one. 
 Amid a hectic day in the Premier League , I find myself sat at the AIG Stadium, the home of League Two leaders Salford City. There is not a cloud in the sky and it is unseasonably warm in Greater Manchester where the Ammies are aiming to secure an eighth straight league win. David Beckham and Gary Neville are part of the ownership and there is plenty of ambition to move up the leagues, despite having the fourth-lowest average attendance.
 Former Ange Postecoglou assistant Peter Cklamovski is in charge of Salford and is redefining their style. They suffered a bumpy start, losing their first three games but they have found their way under the Australian coach and few would back against them winning the league come May.
 Share 2h ago 10.02 EDT This is one of the most pathetic episodes in Premier League history. We’re so over if clubs are taking legal action over some comments on a podcast, get a grip.

 Share 3h ago 09.40 EDT I know this blog is the main event, but if you want a little livener then Scott Murray is on Chelsea v Manchester United, where Morgan Rogers has just given the home side a 1-0 lead:
 Chelsea v Manchester United: Premier League – live Read more View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes fires a shot at as Manchester United take on Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty Images Share 3h ago 09.31 EDT Preamble
 A rare treat with five 3pm kick-offs in the Premier League this afternoon. There’s a Carabao Cup rematch at the Etihad as Brighton aim to get revenge for their defeat on penalties on Wednesday night. Bournemouth look to continue their good form against a resolute Leeds side, Brentford v Forest should be entertaining, there’s a basement battle between Coventry and Sunderland, while two promoted sides go at it with Ipswich on the road at Hull. In the Championship West Ham v West Brom will be worth keeping an eye on, my pick for League One is Mansfield v Notts County, and League Two leaders Salford welcome in-form Exeter to Moor Lane. I’ll be doing my best to keep you across all of it and first up is the team news, in about 15 minutes.
